newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF rallies on privatisation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF rallies on privatisation hopes.

text.p: Shares in state-controlled defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF shot up 4.29 percent on Friday, bolstered by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's comments on Thursday evening that the government would be "flexible" and "not ideological" as far as privatisations were concerned.
Lockheed Martin's plan to take over Northrop Grumman, announced on Thursday, turns up the pressure on Europeans to form competitive defence giants.

"This new deal underscores the competitive nature of this industry, in which Thomson-CSF remains the only non-American supplier of a significant size," brokerage Ferri said in its daily stock comment.
It said it had a very short-term objective of 185 francs for Thomson-CSF, which was trading at 170 francs at 0900 GMT on Friday, up seven francs.

Thomson-CSF chairman Marcel Roulet told the French parliament's defence committee that the group risked being excluded from the European defence industry's restructuring if the French state retained majority control, according to minutes released on Thursday.
Brokers said Thomson-CSF shares were catching up after falling sharply on the change in government.

Jospin's latest remarks were encouraging, they said. "I think that in a certain number of areas, we must look for fairly flexible methods, not to be ideological and not refuse (to accept) industrial reality in the name of non-privatisation, nor seek to privatise systematically ... We will seek, on a case-by-case basis, the best solutions and we will explain them to the French," Jospin said on France 2 television.
"What will guide me is industrial logic, for example in the defence indutry," he added.
